decision: How should How it works show that step 6 leads back to step 2, now that the drawn outline around step 2 (D-047) looks bad?
invariants: same six steps, copy and photos as the live site
no drawn outline on top of a card

options.bet: Keep the return line and dot; step 2 lights up its own border when the dot arrives
options.benefit: Smallest change to the live code; the highlight always fits the card
options.cost: Shows only the jump, not the cycle
options.risk: Still reads as a decorative line

options.bet: A highlight walks through steps 2-6, then the line lights up and carries it back to 2
options.benefit: The motion itself is the cycle; the line only appears when it means something
options.cost: 7.6 s per cycle; the eye has to watch for a while
options.risk: Motion across six photo cards can feel busy

options.bet: Layout says it: Assess once on top, steps 2-6 inside an 'Every book' frame, the sixth slot is a 'back to 02' tile
options.benefit: Readable without animation and on phones; no measuring code
options.cost: Bigger layout change; Assess becomes a wide card
options.risk: The frame may look like a pricing box

options.bet: B plus a 'Book 1 / 2 / 3' counter on Deliver that rolls each time the dot arrives
options.benefit: Shows what the loop means: each lap is a new book
options.risk: The counter can read as a promise about how many books
